prompt: Replacing a library's functions at run time with wrappers is called monkey-___.
Which packages decide what `opentelemetry-instrument` patches in a given service?

choices.text: The libraries the service's code imports at the top of each file
choices.why: Importing a library is not enough; its instrumentation has to be installed.

choices.text: The instrumentation packages installed beside them
choices.why: Right: one per library, loaded if present.

choices.text: A list in the Collector's configuration
choices.why: The Collector is a separate process and patches nothing.

choices.text: `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`
choices.why: That names the service; it chooses nothing.

prompt: What does `opentelemetry-bootstrap` do?

choices.text: It starts the Collector beside the service
choices.why: It never starts processes.

choices.text: It writes spans by hand into the code
choices.why: It touches no source file.

choices.text: It lists instrumentation packages matching what is installed
choices.why: Right, and can install them.

choices.text: It converts old attribute names into new ones
choices.why: That is `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`'s job.

prompt: Match each span in orders to the library that opened it.
The `INSERT` span's `db.statement` shows `%s` where the SKU and total went. Why are the values missing?
hint: How did the code hand them to psycopg?

choices.text: The code passed them as parameters, apart from the query text
choices.why: Right. The instrumentation records the statement it was given.

choices.text: The Collector removes every value that looks like data before storing
choices.why: The lab's Collector does no redaction; lesson 10 adds some.

choices.text: Jaeger hides values unless asked for them
choices.why: It shows what it stored.

choices.text: The values were too long for an attribute
choices.why: They were short; they were never in the statement.

prompt: A dashboard filters spans on `http.request.method = POST` and shows the storefront but not orders. Why?
hint: Compare the attribute names each service sent.

choices.text: orders handles no POST requests
choices.why: It handles `POST /orders`.

choices.text: The filter only works on manual spans
choices.why: A filter matches attributes, whoever set them.

choices.text: Its spans come from an instrumentation still on the older `http.method`
choices.why: Right. Two generations of names are mixed until the opt-in is set.

choices.text: Jaeger drops attributes from services without code
choices.why: It kept sixteen of them.

prompt: The environment variable that switches instrumentations to the stable attribute names is `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY____`.
Why does orders exclude `/health` and `/metrics` from tracing?
hint: Who calls them, and how often?

choices.text: They return errors that would pollute the error rate
choices.why: They answer 200.

choices.text: They are called on a schedule, and would fill the traces with noise
choices.why: Right: a trace every fifteen seconds that nobody wants.

choices.text: Flask cannot trace a route that returns JSON
choices.why: The checkout returns JSON and is traced.

choices.text: They are not routes, so no span exists
choices.why: Both are routes; the exclusion is what removes them.

prompt: With `OTEL_PYTHON_DISABLED_INSTRUMENTATIONS=psycopg`, what happened to the database calls?
hint: Compare the operations before and after.

choices.text: They failed, because the driver was unloaded
choices.why: The checkout succeeded; only the wrapping was skipped.

choices.text: They were traced under `POST /orders` with a new name
choices.why: No new span appeared.

choices.text: They ran as before, with no spans
choices.why: Right. Only the watching was switched off.

choices.text: They went straight to the Collector as metrics
choices.why: Metrics export is off in orders.

prompt: An instrumentation starts producing thousands of useless spans in production. What is the quickest safe response?

choices.text: Rewrite the service with hand-made spans
choices.why: That is weeks of work, not a quick response.

choices.text: Stop the Collector until it is fixed
choices.why: That loses every service's telemetry.

choices.text: Delete the instrumentation package inside the running container and wait for it to notice
choices.why: The patch is already in memory, and the next deploy brings it back.

choices.text: Disable that one instrumentation with its environment variable and restart
choices.why: Right. It silences one library and leaves the rest.

prompt: Which of these does automatic instrumentation of orders NOT record? Choose all that apply.
hint: Edges are seen, the inside is not.

choices.text: Which product was ordered
choices.why: Yes: Flask does not know what an order is.

choices.text: The publish to RabbitMQ
choices.why: Yes: no instrumentation for `pika` is installed.

choices.text: The call to payments
choices.why: That is the `requests` client span.

choices.text: The route that was called
choices.why: `http.route` is there.

choices.text: Whether the order was paid
choices.why: Yes: that is the shop's own logic.

prompt: With the inject line removed, the storefront and the mailer logged different trace ids for one checkout. What does that mean?
hint: Look at the mailer span's parent.

choices.text: The mailer handled a different order
choices.why: It was the same order; only the trace was split.

choices.text: The trace ended at orders, and the mailer began a new one
choices.why: Right. Its consumer span has no parent.

choices.text: Jaeger merged two traces by mistake
choices.why: Nothing was merged; they are two.

choices.text: The queue rejected the message's headers and delivered the body on its own
choices.why: There were no trace headers to reject.

prompt: payments' 1.5 s wait was found in lesson 1 because of a hand-written span. What would the trace have shown without that span?

choices.text: Nothing at all from payments
choices.why: Its `POST /charge` span would still exist.

choices.text: `POST /charge` taking 1501 ms with nothing inside
choices.why: Right. The time is there; the reason is not.

choices.text: An automatic span named `time.sleep`
choices.why: Nothing instruments `time.sleep`.

choices.text: An error, because a span cannot last over a second
choices.why: Spans last as long as the work.

prompt: How did the line added to `create()` reach the span Flask had opened?
hint: Which span is current inside the handler?

choices.text: By opening a new span with the same name
choices.why: No new span is opened.

choices.text: By asking Jaeger for the span id
choices.why: The code never talks to Jaeger.

choices.text: With `trace.get_current_span()`
choices.why: Right. Flask's span is current for the whole request.

choices.text: Through an environment variable read by Flask
choices.why: Attribute values come from the code.

prompt: What does `trace.get_current_span().set_attribute(...)` cost in a process with no SDK?

choices.text: It raises, because there is no span
choices.why: The API never raises for that.

choices.text: Next to nothing
choices.why: Right: it lands on a do-nothing span, which is why the line is safe to leave in.

choices.text: A new trace, started just for the attribute and closed right after it
choices.why: Nothing is recorded without an SDK.

choices.text: One HTTP request to the Collector
choices.why: No exporter exists without an SDK.

prompt: Put the steps of adding `shop.sku` to orders' automatic span in order.
items: Add the import and the `set_attribute` line to `create()`
Restart orders so the mounted code is read again
Read the `POST /orders` span's attributes in Jaeger

prompt: bench.py measured a median of 25.1 ms with instrumentation and 24.1 ms without. How many milliseconds per order did instrumentation add at the median?
Why would the same fixed cost per span matter more on a cache hit answered in 0.1 ms than on an order?
hint: Compare it with the rest of the request.

choices.text: It becomes most of the request's time instead of a small share
choices.why: Right. An order spends 25 ms on real work.

choices.text: Caches are not allowed to be traced
choices.why: Nothing forbids it.

choices.text: A cache hit creates more spans than an order
choices.why: It creates fewer.

choices.text: The batch processor is slower for small requests
choices.why: It works the same whatever the request.

prompt: The benchmark showed a difference of one millisecond in one run of 300. What is the honest conclusion?
hint: How big is the noise between two runs?

choices.text: Instrumentation costs exactly four per cent everywhere
choices.why: One run on one machine says nothing that precise.

choices.text: Instrumentation is free
choices.why: It measured a cost, just a small one.

choices.text: The cost is small, near the noise between runs
choices.why: Right, and the costs worth worrying about are elsewhere.

choices.text: The benchmark is broken and must be rerun until zero
choices.why: A result you dislike is not a broken test.

prompt: Which arrangement does orders end up with, and why is it the usual one?

choices.text: By hand only, because automatic spans use old names
choices.why: orders keeps its automatic spans.

choices.text: Automatic for the edges, plus a few lines for what only the code knows
choices.why: Right: the cheapest way to cover both.

choices.text: Automatic only, because hand-written spans are slower than the ones a library opens
choices.why: Speed is not the difference; coverage is.

choices.text: Neither: it relies on the storefront's spans
choices.why: Each service records its own.

prompt: Java's agent, .NET's launcher and an eBPF tool are all automatic. Which limits do they share with Python's? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: They cannot name a business object
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: They cannot see inside the service's own logic
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: They cannot see HTTP requests
choices.why: Seeing HTTP is exactly what they do well.

choices.text: They cannot follow a client they do not know
choices.why: Yes.
